parsed.explanation: Combined regime is High Risk. Documented traveller-facing exposures include passport sex-marker restrictions (X markers stopped, passports confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded), entry refusal and a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding under a discrepancy-based cable, and state facilities bans covering government buildings in many states. Trespass arrests with handcuffing and 24 hours in a men's ward are documented. Immigration custody shows documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse, and corrections policy removes hormones. National threat-framing names pro-trans groups for 'neutralisation'. Division-level adult care remains partly available and some anti-discrimination and hate-crime protection exists, but these do not offset the national exposures. Violence magnitude is undocumented because only undenominated floor counts are given.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex markers must match birth sex; X markers no longer issued; passports confiscated or blocked at processing; discrepancies trigger refusal, and a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding is possible. Entry screening carries advisory tags for trans athletes.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; a civil-liberties suit is pending and the policy is challenged, though the Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate to refusal, fraud allegation and permanent ineligibility, with stranding abroad. Passport refusal affects the traveller regardless of the division.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Corrections policy from 2026 mandates hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; the bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The national prison LGBTQ-rights order was rescinded, so no custody protection is documented. Litigation is ongoing.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy or arrest can lead into national custody, where the documented harms apply. Division trespass arrests can place a trans person in a men's ward.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Government-funded single-sex facilities restricted nationally. Nine states plus one more bar gender-congruent use of all government buildings; nine more cover schools and some government buildings; three cover schools only. Four states criminalise certain use. Six apply to some private settings. The division's own facilities status is not documented in the division evidence.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Twenty-nine states, four more and the capital district have no mapped ban. The map notes that other sex-defining rules may still apply.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rules are enforced by government staff and interact with ID checks. Trespass arrest requires refusal to leave on request, which the visitor may not be told about in advance.

care_services.exposure: Division law bars licensed clinicians from hormone or surgery for under-18s, with licence revocation possible. A coastal hospital cancelled all gender-affirming surgery in February 2025, including for a 24-year-old adult. National subpoenas of hospital records for under-19s and proposed public-insurance exclusion for under-18s.
care_services.protection: Adult hormone care is not restricted in the dossier. The public-employee plan settlement covers medically necessary care for employees and dependants, with coverage that may extend to minors treated out of state. Visitors cannot use the employee plan.
care_services.interaction: Care records can be subpoenaed nationally. Minors cannot be treated in-division, and a guardian's payment route relies on out-of-state care. Adult surgery capacity depends on outside funding decisions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for 'rapid identification and neutralization'. A cash reward system uses 'radical gender ideology' framing. Executive orders direct investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition. Official framing treats gender identity as a threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states powers will not target people who disagree. Several orders are blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing feeds into facility enforcement and custody practice, raising exposure for visitors who are flagged or detained.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling minor cannot receive transition hormones or surgery from an in-division licensed clinician. Guardians face possible school and records-based prosecution pressure and national subpoenas of care records including names and SSNs. Minors' facility exposure follows the same rules as adults.
minors_guardians.protection: Minors already on hormones before 1 July 2023 may continue. The 2023 ban's enforceability is unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor needing care has no in-division route; out-of-state care is the only payment path. Records can be pulled federally. Minors in custody face placement and treatment exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A major city recorded two fatal shootings of Black trans women a week apart and a January 2023 critical shooting, with three open investigations and officials calling the violence epidemic-level. The public trespass arrest in a capitol was handcuffed and held in a men's ward.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police opened investigations and the outcomes of the 2023 cases are not recorded. Hate-crime coverage exists nationally, and 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw counts lack a denominator and the floor-based rate is not used, so the violence magnitude against trans visitors is undocumented and no elevated risk can be inferred from the counts.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Anti-discrimination protection covers 22 states plus the capital district. Remedies against the passport restrictions, national orders and the division's 2023 ban are pending or enjoined. Division-level trespass and the facilities statute's status are not confirmed for this division. Whether the coastal hospital's suspension is permanent is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Enjoined national orders; a pending passport suit; a 2023 employee-plan settlement that applies to residents only; hate-crime and anti-discrimination statutes operating unevenly.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is slow and uneven, and the state running oversight also runs the custody and border exposures, so recourse does not reduce the documented exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in having birth-sex facility and custody rules, abuse in custody, and entry or stop-based extortion risk. This case is comparable on severity: documented immigration-custody sexual abuse and medication removal. It is not lower on passport refusal and lifetime fraud exposure. It sits slightly higher because the division's adult care and anti-discrimination coverage partly operate.

Similar in birth-sex facility and emergency-ward exposure with no documented pass-through for passports. This case is lower because it adds national custody abuse, medication denial and state threat-framing, while 0.35-A has no documented custody abuse or threat-framing. It is higher because adult care and protections partly operate.

Lower-severity than 0.15-D: no registry, no state-run extortion of visitors and no documented routine custody sentencing for presentation. It is closer to 0.25-D in severity because of documented custody abuse and national threat-framing, but it remains well above the severe band.

Lower than 0.45-B because the dossier documents passport and entry exposure and documented abuse in immigration custody, which 0.45-B's accepted documents and oversight-only custody issue does not show. Higher only where anti-discrimination and adult care are operating in the division.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's principal exposure is documents and entry: a non-matching passport can be refused, detained or made the basis of a permanent ineligibility finding. Facilities rules bind in many states, and trespass arrests are documented. If the traveller is detained, immigration and corrections custody show documented abuse, forced labour and medication removal. The division adds a minor-care ban and a hospital adult-surgery cancellation, but adult hormone care and anti-discrimination law still provide partial mitigation. State threat-framing and enjoined orders make the exposure unstable. Violence magnitude is undocumented.
